findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permissions, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing input path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed domain error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> or a typed domain error, propagate with ?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value or out-of-range input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row crashes the program instead of returning a parse error
findings.fix: use parse::<u32>() with map_err to return a typed parse error, then convert to u16 with u16::try_from

findings.problem: Lossy `as` cast from u32 to u16: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 like 70000 becomes 4444 with no error, corrupting data silently
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap_or_else(|_| return Err(...))) or parse directly with checked arithmetic and return an error

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() into Vec<String> when split_once suffices for two-field CSV
findings.failure_mode: allocates a full Vec and clones every field string even though only the first two fields are needed; extra allocations on every line
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name, rest) directly, trim name, parse rest

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into Vec<String> - if line has fewer than 2 comma-separated fields, parts[0] exists but parts[1] panics at line 19; also index access into a heap-allocated Vec is not zero-cost
findings.failure_mode: short line like "foo" causes parts.len() == 1, then parts[1] at line 19 panics via index out of bounds
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') and match; if no second field, return a typed error

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing into Vec<String> allocated by collect
findings.failure_mode: index out of bounds on short lines instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: replace with split_once(',') pattern and match on Some((name, value_str))

findings.problem: println! side effect inside data-loading logic that is not a pure calculation
findings.failure_mode: I/O coupling makes the function harder to test deterministically; logging is mixed into data parsing pipeline
findings.fix: remove println!; if logging is needed, push it to the shell layer outside the data-loading function

findings.problem: load_orders mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string, println) with data parsing in a single public function with no error surface
findings.failure_mode: cannot test parsing logic in isolation; no typed error distinction between I/O failures, parse failures, and domain errors
findings.fix: split into: (1) pure fn parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError>, (2) shell fn load_orders(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that handles fs::read_to_string and maps errors

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 with no domain invariants enforced; value: u16 accepts 0 which may be invalid in context
findings.failure_mode: illegal values (e.g., zero, negative via unsigned wrapping) can be constructed without validation
findings.fix: use newtypes like RecordName(String) and a value type with a constructor that validates invariants, or add a Record::try_new constructor

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_orders performance on expected input sizes
no profiler data for allocation profile of the split/collect pipeline
no allocation analysis showing Vec<String> allocations per line
no second-ring evidence (Kani/property tests) for parsing invariants
no command evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. The crate has 9 blocker-level violations spanning unwrap/panic, unchecked indexing, lossy casts, missing error types, I/O in core logic, and absent benchmarks. All I/O (fs, println) must be pulled to a shell layer, all unwrap/as must become Result with typed errors, and split_once must replace the collect-based split pattern.
